Independence note: mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder retained (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and full-span slats to achieve required lift at low speed; inputs: crew/system command; processing: two independent power drive units through common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes; outputs: high-lift position to performance computation. Independence note: common torque shaft is a recorded commonality (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of positioning aerodynamic surfaces to achieve commanded flight path and attitude across the envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Gear supports the aircraft and spreads footprint pressure to the level semi-prepared surfaces require; inputs: hydraulic A for retract/extend, free-fall alternate; processing: bogie/tyre flotation sizing; outputs: gear position, weight-on-wheels to many consumers. fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust from a single engine at the 28 m outboard moment arm produces a yawing/rolling moment; a step change at low speed drives asymmetry toward the directional-control sizing case. Aircraft trajectory disturbed pending crew recognition and rudder/throttle response.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to recognise the uncommanded change, identify the affected engine and re-trim; rudder input to counter yaw.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the magnitude, direction (thrust rise vs decay) and which engine, none of which are quantified in the SDD; an uncommanded surge on an outboard engine near V1 could approach the directional-control sizing case (potentially Hazardous) while a small inboard change may be Minor. Magnitude/engine data required to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to a crew thrust command (engine responds other than as commanded)
fha.effAc: Commanded thrust not delivered as intended; if erroneous response is asymmetric between engines at the 28 m moment arm, yawing/rolling moment develops. Trajectory and speed control degraded until the crew detects the discrepancy against displayed engine parameters.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to reconcile lever position against actual engine response and to compensate for any asymmetry.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The magnitude and symmetry of the erroneous response are not quantified in the SDD, and the outcome ranges from a Minor mismatch to an asymmetric excursion near the directional-control sizing case; cannot classify without the response magnitude and number of engines affected.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow thrust drift below the crew detection threshold, crew unaware
fha.effAc: A slow drift below the crew threshold, with the crew continuing normal duties and taking no action, produces a gradual asymmetry or thrust/fuel-schedule error that accumulates unnoticed; effect on trajectory is initially small but may reach a noticeable asymmetry or performance shortfall over time.
fha.effCrew: By definition unaware; no immediate action taken, so no added workload until the drift eventually becomes perceptible or crosses an alerting threshold.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected drift rate, the eventual bound before any alert, and whether it can grow into an asymmetry approaching the directional-control sizing case are not quantified in the SDD; classification requires the drift magnitude/rate and the detection-threshold assumption.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust (one engine) with resulting directional-control asymmetry, within available control authority
fha.effAc: Loss of one engine at or after V1 produces asymmetric thrust; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine, so with rudder authority sized to the outboard 28 m moment-arm case the crew retains control at reduced climb/performance margins. Significant reduction in performance and safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload to identify the failed engine, apply rudder to counter yaw, re-trim, run the engine-out procedure and revise performance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one engine is a designed-for dispatch case that the aircraft is stated to continue to a suitable aerodrome from, at reduced margins and significantly increased crew workload — a significant reduction in functional capabilities and significant increase in crew workload, i.e. Major (proposed, engineer to confirm at the worst applicable phase). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Asymmetric reverse thrust during the ground roll produces a yawing moment tending to swing the aircraft toward the reduced-reverse side, degrading directional control on a semi-prepared strip during deceleration.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload correcting the induced yaw via steering/braking while managing rollout within the available landing distance.
fha.effPax: No passengers in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function alone: the severity turns on whether the induced yaw and asymmetric deceleration can be contained within the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing distance requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, which requires directional-control and stopping-distance analysis not derivable from the function definition. NOTE: this condition is not present in the current SF-002 FCIM rows — engineer to confirm it should be carried.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust contribution during the ground roll; deceleration relies more heavily on wheel braking, eroding the margin between the 1,800 m landing distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Increased attention to stopping performance and braking management during rollout.
fha.effPax: No passengers in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function alone: reverse thrust is a supplementary decelerator and the effect depends on whether wheel braking alone contains the aircraft within the required landing distance on the operating surface — a stopping-distance analysis outside the function definition. Leaving severity empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust contribution to the ground roll; deceleration depends entirely on wheel braking (and any spoilers) against the 1,800 m landing distance requirement versus ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface, reducing the stopping margin.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload and reliance on the braking system to stop within the available distance; potential need to manage an eroded margin on an unprepared strip.
fha.effPax: No passengers in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function alone: whether total loss of reverse deceleration reduces the stopping margin to an overrun risk depends on the braking system's contribution and the surface, which requires a landing-distance/overrun analysis not derivable from the function definition. Leaving severity empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of reverse thrust for ground deceleration, unannunciated at deceleration onset (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration relies on wheel braking without the reverse-thrust contribution; stopping distance increases. Reverse is fitted to inboard engines only and the deceleration design case rests on wheel braking against the stated margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout).
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal rollout with no annunciation and takes no compensating action for the reverse-thrust loss.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity without the braking/performance interaction: whether reverse-thrust loss alone erodes the 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m margin below the required landing distance (particularly on the semi-prepared surface) is not established by the function definition. Left empty pending performance/braking analysis rather than assuming benign.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous aircraft attitude response to crew command in pitch, roll or yaw (crew aware)
fha.effAc: The aircraft responds to control commands with erroneous attitude, degrading control of the flight path; controllability is impaired across the envelope, worst at low altitude and high workload.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware through display/aircraft response mismatch and must counter the erroneous response, with a large increase in workload and potential inability to maintain the intended trajectory.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous attitude response is a direct impairment of controlled flight; at low altitude the crew may be unable to arrest the resulting flight-path deviation, entailing loss of the airplane. Proposed for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow uncommanded aircraft attitude divergence below the crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded attitude divergence develops below the crew's detection threshold; the aircraft departs from the intended trajectory without correction until the divergence becomes significant.
fha.effCrew: Crew is unaware and continues normal duties, taking no corrective action; by the time the divergence is detectable the recovery margin may be reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected attitude divergence removes the crew's opportunity to arrest it early; an unchecked divergence can develop into loss of control before intervention, entailing loss of the airplane. Proposed for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move without command, creating a configuration/speed mismatch; the aircraft effect depends on the phase and airspeed at which movement occurs (structural overspeed if extended at high speed, or lift/drag loss if retracted at low speed).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft effect of uncommanded movement is bounded by the flight phase and airspeed at which it occurs and by the placard/envelope limits, none of which are fixed by the function definition or the SDD. Provide the high-lift airspeed envelope / overspeed case to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability — aircraft supported on the ground but at reduced footprint/load-spreading or reduced gear function
fha.effAc: Reduced ground-support/flotation margin; on a semi-prepared strip a partial loss of load-spreading raises the risk of gear sinkage, veer or asymmetric support during rollout, eroding the margin between the 1,080 m predicted rollout and the 1,800 m requirement.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control and manage a degraded ground configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the severity from the function definition alone: 'partial loss of ground support' spans a wide range from a single degraded bogie (likely Minor/Major) to loss of load-spreading on an unprepared surface (potentially higher). The specific degradation extent and its effect on stopping/directional margin are not stated at aircraft-function level; needs the SFHA (LDG) to bound the partial case before a class is defensible.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of adequate flotation on a semi-prepared surface — footprint pressure exceeds what the operating surface will bear
fha.effAc: Gear sinkage / rutting on the semi-prepared strip; potential gear collapse, veer-off or an aborted/failed rollout. On a surface sized around the flotation the tyres were chosen to achieve, loss of flotation directly threatens the ability to complete the landing rollout within the available surface.
fha.effCrew: High workload attempting to maintain directional control and arrest the aircraft on a degrading surface; limited effective crew mitigation once flotation is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects plausibly range from a significant reduction in ground safety margins up to loss of the aircraft in a gear-collapse/veer-off, but the outcome depends on surface state, weight and speed at onset — none fixed at aircraft-function level. The flotation basis (1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout) is preliminary/given data, not validated. Severity left empty pending SFHA and the substantiated flotation case rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support and flotation capability — the aircraft cannot be supported on the ground by any means
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be supported on the ground: at touchdown or on take-off roll this is a gear-down/collapse scenario with loss of the airplane and structural breakup.
fha.effCrew: No effective crew mitigation available for total loss of ground support at touchdown.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the ability to support the aircraft on the ground at landing/take-off entails loss of the airplane; per the closed anchor set this is Catastrophic. Objective for confirmation: Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh (Part 25). Engineer to confirm class and phase applicability. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Braking erroneously applied against crew command — braking action differs from the crew's braking command
fha.effAc: Erroneous braking contrary to command (e.g. braking applied when release is commanded, or asymmetric application) degrades stopping and can induce a veer-off or asymmetric deceleration on the semi-prepared strip, eroding the rollout margin. During a high-speed take-off roll erroneous braking is a rejected/asymmetric-deceleration hazard.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and counter braking that does not follow the command, and to maintain directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects span from a manageable asymmetric-deceleration event (workload-driven, likely Major) to a directional-loss/veer-off at high energy (potentially higher). The extent and symmetry of the erroneous braking, and the speed at onset, are not fixed at aircraft-function level; anti-skid per-wheel-pair architecture and the SFHA are needed to bound worst case before committing a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground wheel-braking deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel-braking deceleration on the ground; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout the stopping margin is lost and a runway overrun is likely, aggravated by the unprepared surface beyond the strip; reverse thrust (inboard reversers only) and accumulator-supported emergency braking remain but are not credited in this loss.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an imminent overrun with limited alternate deceleration means and high workload to manage it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed to overrun outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: At the landing/RTO sizing case the braking margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout) is the operating basis; total loss of wheel braking on a semi-prepared strip removes that margin and an overrun off the prepared surface can result in loss of the airplane. Proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation; residual deceleration from reversers/accumulator braking may support a lower class and must be assessed. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced braking with degraded stopping performance
fha.effAc: Wheel braking available but at reduced effectiveness, increasing stopping distance and eroding the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout; overrun risk on the semi-prepared surface rises with the degree of degradation.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive degraded stopping and must manage remaining deceleration means and stopping-distance judgement under increased workload.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no in-flight occupants in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Class depends on how much stopping distance is lost against the ~720 m margin — a small reduction is a significant reduction in safety margins (Major), a large reduction approaching the available strip length trends toward Hazardous, and total consumption of margin toward an overrun. The SDD does not quantify the braking degradation for this condition, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be pinned to one class. Left empty pending the degraded-braking stopping-distance analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded braking effectiveness below crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Stopping performance is degraded but the loss is below the threshold at which the crew detect it; the crew continue normally and take no corrective action, so the stopping-distance margin against the 1,800 m requirement is silently reduced, discovered only late in the ground roll if the degradation is enough to threaten the overrun boundary.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding the undetected degradation; late recognition compresses time to react.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no in-flight occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — By definition the degradation is below crew-detection threshold and small; the aircraft effect depends on how much margin a sub-threshold loss can consume against the ~720 m stopping margin, which the SDD does not quantify. Cannot be grounded to a single class without the detection-threshold and stopping-distance data. Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Anti-skid regulation error not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Anti-skid regulates braking incorrectly (per wheel pair) without the crew being aware; erroneous modulation can lock or under-brake wheels on the semi-prepared surface, degrading stopping performance and/or inducing directional asymmetry, with the crew continuing normally and taking no corrective action.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the regulation error, continue normal braking; no corrective action taken for the true condition.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no in-flight occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a slight stopping-distance penalty to a directional/asymmetry event depending on how the anti-skid mis-regulates and how many wheel pairs are affected — the SDD states anti-skid is per-wheel-pair but does not characterise the erroneous-regulation behaviour or its detection, so the aircraft-level effect and its worst-case class cannot be grounded. Left empty pending the anti-skid failure-behaviour analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Small uncommanded nose-wheel steering bias not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: A small steady bias below the crew-detection threshold produces a gradual directional drift the crew correct as part of tracking the centreline; the drift is bounded and slow relative to the available lateral room on the strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the bias source; continue normal directional tracking with slightly increased steering input; no discrete alert assumed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the magnitude of the undetected bias, the lateral room available on the semi-prepared strip, and whether an unaware crew can hold the centreline within surface limits are not stated in the provided material. Confirm the bounded bias magnitude and surface lateral margin before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority or range
fha.effAc: Reduced steering authority degrades directional control precision on the ground; the aircraft remains steerable but with less margin to correct excursions on the narrow semi-prepared strip, and differential braking must supplement directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew compensate with differential braking and pedal input; increased workload and reduced precision, with the degradation annunciated (aware case).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the residual authority available after the reduction, and whether differential braking preserves adequate directional control within the strip's lateral limits, are not quantified in the provided material. Confirm residual authority and available compensation before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric or restricted directional (nose-wheel steering) response
fha.effAc: An asymmetric or one-sided steering response biases the aircraft toward one side and limits correction in that direction; on the narrow semi-prepared strip this reduces the room to keep the aircraft on the prepared surface and shifts directional-control reliance onto differential braking.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the asymmetry and compensate with differential braking and pedal input against a directional bias; increased workload at a critical ground phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the degree of asymmetry/restriction and the residual controllability with differential braking on the strip are not stated in the provided material. Confirm before classifying. NOTE: this condition is not currently in the SF-007 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded nose-wheel steering response below crew-detection threshold — reduced directional-control precision on the ground not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Reduced precision of ground directional control; small lateral-tracking errors uncorrected because below the crew-detection threshold. On a semi-prepared strip with predicted rollout ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m requirement the lateral margin is narrow, giving a slight reduction in the ground safety margin.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload to hold centreline; no annunciation, so the crew compensate by continuous manual correction.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects entail a slight reduction in ground directional safety margin and a slight workload increase, with the degradation below the crew-detection threshold and other directional means (rudder/differential braking) available — supports Minor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering directional control on the ground
fha.effAc: Loss of nose-wheel steering directional control; ground directional control must be maintained by rudder and differential braking alone. On a semi-prepared strip with a narrow lateral margin this is a significant reduction in ground-handling safety margin, with increased risk of runway departure.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to maintain track using rudder and differential braking with reduced authority at low ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects entail a significant reduction in ground directional safety margin and a significant increase in crew workload, with alternate directional means (rudder, differential braking) remaining — supports Major. Whether an outside-margin runway-departure case on the semi-prepared strip escalates to Hazardous requires the flight-control directional-control sizing and ground-handling analysis, which the SDD does not provide. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated locked to the crew when not fully secured
fha.effAc: The nose visor forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward-fuselage structural load path when closed; if it is dispatched believed locked while not fully secured, in-flight opening or loss of the pressure boundary and forward load path could result in loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Erroneous locked indication defeats the flight-deck lock status and the take-off configuration check; the crew have no cue and take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew, who are exposed to the loss-of-airplane outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The door is a pressure-boundary and forward structural load-path element; a false locked indication with no crew cue can lead to in-flight door loss and loss of the airplane — the effects entail the Catastrophic anchor. Final classification depends on the door structural / pressure-boundary and PRA substantiation, not established here. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Incomplete nose-door lock engagement not detected by either sensing path
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths fail to reveal incomplete pin engagement; the visor may be dispatched with the pressure boundary and forward structural load path not fully secured, and in-flight opening or loss of that boundary could result in loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Neither the proximity sensing harness nor the mechanical indicator reveals the condition; the crew have no cue from either path and take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew, who are exposed to the loss-of-airplane outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected incomplete lock engagement of a pressure-boundary and forward structural load-path element, with both sensing paths blind, can lead to in-flight door loss and loss of the airplane — the effects entail the Catastrophic anchor. Final classification depends on the door structural / pressure-boundary and PRA substantiation, not established here. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Payload restraint status erroneously indicated intact when degraded
fha.effAc: Crew are not alerted to a degraded restraint state on a single 72.6 t unitised blade; the aircraft-level consequence of undetected restraint degradation on controllability, CG excursion or structural load path is not stated in the provided material.
fha.effCrew: No indication of the degraded condition; crew continue normal duties and take no action, consistent with the false-intact indication.
fha.effPax: No occupant effect; the hold is not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD describes the restraint architecture but does not state the aircraft-level effect of an undetected degraded restraint (blade-shift dynamics, CG excursion limit, or structural consequence). Needs engineering judgment / analysis on blade shift and CG to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint tension monitoring loop failed such that degradation goes unannunciated
fha.effAc: The single instrumented tension monitoring loop no longer annunciates strap-tension loss; a subsequent restraint degradation on the 72.6 t blade would proceed undetected. The aircraft-level consequence of an undetected restraint degradation is not stated in the provided material.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of restraint condition; crew have in-flight indication only and no in-flight means of adjustment, so they continue normal duties.
fha.effPax: No occupant effect; the hold is not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: this is a latent loss of monitoring coverage. The SDD notes the loop is a single instrumented run whose coverage is a recorded item, but does not state the aircraft-level effect of an undetected restraint failure. Severity depends on the combination with a restraint degradation and on blade-shift/CG consequence, neither quantified here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded payload restraint at one or more stations within capability
fha.effAc: Loss of a strap at a station is designed to be carried by its neighbours; loss of two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. The aircraft-level consequence (margin consumed against load cases, CG or controllability) of restraint degradation within capability is not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effCrew: Crew are annunciated of the degraded restraint condition (single-strap loss annunciated in flight; two adjacent stations annunciated as requiring immediate attention); crew have indication only with no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: No occupant effect; the hold is not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states single-strap loss is carried by neighbours and is annunciated, but does not state the aircraft-level safety-margin reduction of within-capability restraint degradation. Needs the quantified margin against the design load cases to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: complete loss of payload restraint through load cases
fha.effAc: Uncommanded shift of a single unitised 72.6 t blade along/across the 108 m hold; with no redundancy in the hold floor hard points a shift produces a large adverse centre-of-gravity excursion and structural loading outside the design envelope, threatening loss of control and loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Rapid, possibly uncontrollable CG/attitude divergence beyond crew capacity to compensate.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single 72.6 t blade occupying the full hold length, unrestrained, drives a CG and structural excursion the SDD flags as sized by this payload; effects entail loss of the airplane. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: loss of tension at a single strap station
fha.effAc: Loss of one strap; load path sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so restraint is retained at reduced margin. Condition is annunciated in flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to a single-strap tension loss; assessment and monitoring workload; no immediate control effect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Load-path is sized to carry the loss of any one strap on its neighbours and the loss is annunciated, so the effect is a slight reduction in restraint safety margin with monitoring workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: restraint degradation outside the tension-loop coverage
fha.effAc: Restraint degradation in a region not instrumented by the single tension monitoring loop; degradation progresses unannunciated and could, if it propagates across stations, approach a partial or complete loss of restraint of the unitised blade.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification requires how much restraint capability is lost before the degradation becomes detectable by another means and whether it can propagate to a multi-station loss; the SDD records the loop coverage as an open item and does not bound the uncovered degradation, so the aircraft effect cannot be established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: erroneous conditioning or pressurisation control response
fha.effAc: Erroneous pressurisation control response commands an incorrect differential; independent positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure regardless of the control system, bounding the structural outcome.
fha.effCrew: Annunciated abnormal cabin/hold pressure; crew intervene via manual pressurisation mode and, if needed, don crew oxygen; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight deck occupants exposed to a cabin-altitude excursion mitigated by crew oxygen and manual control.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous differential control is annunciated and bounded by independent mechanical relief and by manual reversion; effect is a significant increase in crew workload / conditions impairing efficiency with cabin-altitude exposure the crew can manage. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: erroneous differential control developing below detection threshold
fha.effAc: Erroneous differential develops slowly below the crew detection threshold and unannunciated; crew take no action; independent mechanical relief still protects the structure against over/under-pressure, but a slow cabin-altitude drift may go uncorrected.
fha.effCrew: Unaware condition — crew continue normal duties and take no action; a slow cabin-altitude drift could reach a level affecting crew performance before being noticed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight deck occupants exposed to an undetected slow cabin-altitude change.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the effect turns on how far the undetected differential can drift before independent relief or another cue intervenes, and on the flight-deck cabin-altitude the drift reaches — neither is stated. Provided data (independent relief exists; hold pressurisation differential is preliminary) does not bound the occupant exposure of the unaware case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution to occupied compartments (aware)
fha.effAc: No conditioned air to the flight deck; flight-deck compartment cannot be maintained. With loss of distribution the crew descend to a breathable altitude and divert; crew oxygen is available on donning per OXY. Hold is unoccupied and requires no conditioning for occupants.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck conditioning; crew don oxygen masks (OXY) and initiate descent/diversion, increased workload during the reconfiguration and descent.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight — hold is unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects hinge on whether flight-crew oxygen and emergency descent fully cover loss of conditioning at FL260 without a large reduction in safety margins; the AFHA function definition and SDD do not establish the residual crew-protection duration or the failure of conditioning-plus-distribution combined effect. Cannot derive a class without that; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous over-pressurisation of the occupied compartment (aware)
fha.effAc: Differential control erroneously drives toward over-pressurisation. Independent positive pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, limiting differential to the structural relief setting; crew reconfigure to manual mode. Structural over-pressure is precluded by the independent relief.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to abnormal differential/cabin-altitude indication and revert to manual pressurisation control; increased workload.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight — hold is unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With independent mechanical relief limiting differential the structural outcome is precluded, but the residual severity depends on the relief setting relative to structural margins and on the flight-deck occupant effect of an over-pressure transient before relief acts — the AFHA function definition and SDD low-differential (preliminary) hold value do not establish those margins. Cannot derive a class; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous electrical heating activation reducing available electrical capacity
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the stabiliser/probe heating is electrically supplied but does not state the available electrical margin, what load erroneous heating displaces, or any resulting loss of a function — so no aircraft-level effect can be derived and the condition cannot be classified. Need: electrical capacity margin and the consumers that would be shed if heating is erroneously drawn.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of electrical ice protection across heated zones and elements
fha.effAc: In icing conditions, one or more heated zones/elements (a stabiliser zone, a probe/port, or the windshield) are unprotected while others remain, producing localised ice accretion: a reduced-margin condition or, if a probe is affected, corruption of one air-data source.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone is annunciated per the design; crew respond by exiting icing/altering configuration. Effect depends on which element is lost and whether an air-data source is affected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single aircraft effect: the SDD states six independently controlled stabiliser zones plus individually monitored probes/ports/windshields, so severity depends on WHICH element(s) are lost and whether a heated probe (air data) is among them. Which-element decomposition is needed before a class is derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of heating on an individually monitored probe, port or element
fha.effAc: With the crew unaware, an unheated probe/port ices in icing conditions and its air-data output degrades or freezes; because the individual-element monitor is assumed failed/silent for this condition, misleading air data may enter the displays and envelope protection without a heater fault flag.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally and take no action; they may act on misleading air data before recognising it, since the element-level monitoring that would prompt action is absent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect hinges on WHICH monitored element is lost undetected: an unheated air-data probe feeding misleading airspeed/altitude/AoA points toward Hazardous, whereas a single stabiliser zone or windshield element undetected points lower. The SDD says elements are monitored individually but does not fix which element this condition concerns, so a single class cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading primary flight, navigation or system information presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Crew acts on erroneous but plausible primary flight/nav data with no annunciation; potential loss of control or controlled flight into terrain/obstacle.
fha.effCrew: No alert; crew flies to false indications and cannot detect the error without cross-check against the independent standby instrument.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight data acted upon can lead to loss of the airplane; no independent monitor stated in the description that would annunciate the error before crew action. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight, navigation and system information
fha.effAc: Reduced set of primary information available; aircraft remains controllable using remaining displays/reversionary formats.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload and cross-checking to reconstitute the lost information from remaining sources; degraded state annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss with any-display-any-format reversion and standby available yields a significant increase in crew workload / significant reduction in functional capability, not a large one; extent depends on which formats are lost. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary flight, navigation and system information with independent standby information available
fha.effAc: Primary displays lost; flight continued on the independent integrated standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude) which shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload flying on standby-only information; degraded navigation/system awareness; crew aware.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit: severity turns on whether the independent standby's coverage (attitude/airspeed/altitude only, no nav/system data) is validated sufficient to continue safe flight and land, and on which primary formats are lost — not established in the provided description.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight, navigation and system information
fha.effAc: All primary flight/nav/system information lost; flight relies solely on the independent standby instrument, which provides attitude, airspeed and altitude only and no navigation or system status.
fha.effCrew: Large increase in workload; crew flies on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude with no primary situational or system information; safe continuation and landing significantly challenged.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary information leaves only the independent standby (attitude/airspeed/altitude); a large reduction in functional capability with excessive workload — Hazardous rather than Catastrophic because a validated independent standby remains; confirm standby adequacy. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous alert presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Crew presented a false or incorrect alert; possible inappropriate crew response (e.g. unnecessary shutdown/configuration change) driving the aircraft toward an unsafe state.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload diagnosing a nuisance/false alert; risk of acting on a false condition or distrusting a valid one.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a single severity: outcome ranges from a nuisance (Minor) to a serious inappropriate crew response (potentially Hazardous) depending on which alert is falsely presented and the action it commands; the description does not bound the alert set or the crew action, so severity is left empty for engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Alert presented with incorrect priority
fha.effAc: An existing alert is presented but ranked incorrectly relative to concurrent alerts, so a higher-consequence condition may be actioned late or a lower one actioned first; the aircraft-level effect depends on which conditions are mis-ordered.
fha.effCrew: Crew may address a less urgent condition ahead of a more urgent one; increased workload and potential for a delayed response to the more critical failure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity without knowing which alerts can be mis-prioritised and the consequence of the resulting delayed response; the prioritisation/consequence pairing is not defined at aircraft-function level. Severity left empty pending the alert-priority scheme and the failures whose delayed response drives the effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: False fire, overheat or smoke warning presented with no actual event
fha.effAc: Aircraft is airworthy; crew may take unnecessary action (engine/APU shutdown, extinguisher discharge, diversion) in response to a spurious warning.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload executing a fire/overheat drill for a non-event; potential unnecessary engine shutdown reducing available thrust/redundancy.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct effect on the flight crew beyond workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A spurious warning drives an unnecessary fire drill and possible precautionary engine/APU shutdown, giving a significant increase in crew workload and a reduction in available functional capability — but no immediate hazard to the airframe. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate a genuine detected fire, overheat or smoke event
fha.effAc: A real fire or overheat in an engine, APU or monitored zone progresses without crew awareness; extinguishing is a crew action and is not initiated, allowing fire to develop in a fire zone containing flammable fluid.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of an active fire; no fire drill initiated; awareness only from secondary cues after significant progression.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied; effect is on the airframe and flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected progression of a genuine engine/APU-zone fire without crew action is a large reduction in safety margins; classified Hazardous pending fire-zone effects analysis. NOTE: could be Catastrophic if analysis shows uncontained fire propagation leading to loss of the airplane — engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Silent loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection capability with no fault annunciation
fha.effAc: Detection is unavailable in one or more zones without the crew being alerted; a subsequent fire/overheat in an affected fire zone would go undetected and unextinguished.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware detection coverage is degraded; no compensating vigilance or configuration change taken; a real event would not annunciate.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied; effect is on the airframe and flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A silent loss of detection removes the means by which a fire in a flammable-fluid fire zone would be caught and acted upon; equivalent exposure to an undetected fire — large reduction in safety margins. Confirm whether fire-zone effects analysis pushes this to Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in one or more monitored zones
fha.effAc: Detection lost in a subset of monitored zones while remaining zones stay covered; consequence depends on which zone loses coverage and whether the loss is annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied; effect is on the airframe and flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: the aircraft-level effect of losing detection in an unspecified subset of zones depends on WHICH zone (engine/APU fire zone vs hold vs bleed/gear overheat), whether the loss is crew-annunciated, and the dual-loop degraded logic. The function statement does not establish that consequence. Requires zonal effects analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage
fha.effAc: Overheat detection lost on the bleed duct runs and in the main gear bays; a bleed-duct overheat or gear-bay overheat would progress without detection.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied; effect is on the airframe and flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: the SDD states overheat detection is fitted to the bleed duct runs and main gear bays but does not establish the aircraft-level outcome of an undetected bleed-duct or gear-bay overheat (structural/duct damage severity, propagation potential). Requires effects analysis and PRA/ZSA input to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection along the hold (one or more of the nine hold stations)
fha.effAc: Smoke/fire in the affected hold region is not detected. The hold carries a single blade with no combustible palletised load and no fitted suppression; portable extinguishers are available at the hold access door. Undetected in-flight development of a hold fire is the effect to be assessed.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of a hold event at the affected station(s); crew unaware of a developing condition until it is evident by other means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft-level severity: the SDD states the hold carries a single blade with no combustible palletised load and no suppression, but gives no combustible-fire exposure or ignition-source data from which to establish the consequence of an UNDETECTED hold fire. That likelihood/consequence input is engineering judgement the document does not supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of a detection loop below warning threshold
fha.effAc: A detection loop degrades silently so coverage in the affected zone is lost without fault indication; a subsequent fire or overheat in that zone would not be annunciated. Dual-loop AND logic degrades to single-loop on loss of one loop, so first-loop degradation is nominally covered, but degradation below warning threshold without fault indication removes that margin.
fha.effCrew: No fault indication; crew believe detection coverage is intact when it is degraded.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight deck occupied by crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the effect depends on coincident occurrence of an undetected fire/overheat in the affected zone, and the SDD provides no exposure or coincident-event data to establish the aircraft consequence. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection in all monitored zones
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in any monitored zone: engine nacelles, APU compartment, bleed duct runs, main gear bays and hold. A fire in an engine or APU fire zone would develop without warning; crew-commanded extinguishing depends on that warning. Loss of detection removes the trigger for both crew action and automatic APU discharge.
fha.effCrew: No fire/overheat warning to the crew alerting system for any zone; crew cannot initiate fire-handle extinguishing in response to an undetected engine or APU fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The effect (an undetected engine/APU fire developing without warning) points toward a large reduction in safety margins, but committing a class requires the coincident-fire exposure the SDD does not provide; the document explicitly does not classify anything. Severity left empty for engineering judgement rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge into an engine or APU zone with no fire present
fha.effAc: Extinguishant discharged into a nacelle or the APU compartment with no fire. Agent for that engine pair (two bottles cross-plumbed) or the single APU bottle is expended and unavailable for a subsequent real fire in the affected zone; automatic APU discharge on APU fire would find the bottle spent. No immediate loss of thrust from the discharge itself.
fha.effCrew: Spurious discharge indication; crew must manage the loss of available agent and confirm no fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is loss of available fire-suppression agent in one zone (recoverable pending a subsequent fire), but deriving the aircraft-level class requires the likelihood of a coincident real fire in that zone, which the SDD does not supply. Severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge extinguishant into an engine or APU zone on crew fire-handle command
fha.effAc: With a confirmed engine or APU fire, the crew fire-handle command fails to discharge agent into the affected zone; the fire is not suppressed by the fixed system. Two bottles per engine pair are cross-plumbed so either can serve either nacelle of the pair, and the APU has a single dedicated bottle; a failure defeating discharge on demand leaves an unsuppressed fire in a fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands discharge and it does not occur; no fixed means to extinguish the confirmed fire remains for that zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An unsuppressed engine/APU fire is a serious effect, but its aircraft-level class depends on fire progression/containment and coincident-fire exposure data the SDD does not provide; the document explicitly leaves classification to the safety assessment. Severity left empty rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing in engine and APU zones (detection remains available)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: On a detected engine or APU fire, no agent can be discharged into any protected zone; fire cannot be extinguished by the aircraft means and depends on shutdown/fuel isolation and airflow alone. If the fire is not otherwise arrested it may propagate beyond the nacelle firewall toward wing/fuel structure.
fha.effCrew: Crew actuate fire handles (shutdown, fuel and hydraulic isolation) but obtain no discharge; workload elevated managing an uncontrolled fire and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the coincident engine/APU fire event and whether it becomes uncontained. The SDD gives no fire-growth, firewall-containment or burn-through data, so the aircraft-level outcome (loss of airplane vs. contained) cannot be derived from the function definition. Classify once the coincident-fire consequence is established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced extinguishing capability in a protected zone
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced agent quantity or discharge effectiveness available to a protected zone; on a detected fire the discharge may not fully suppress or may leave the aircraft with no reserve for a re-flash, reducing the margin against an uncontained fire.
fha.effCrew: Crew actuate the fire handle; discharge occurs but effectiveness/reserve is degraded, with elevated workload monitoring for re-flash and planning diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether reduced extinguishing translates to an aircraft effect depends on the coincident fire and whether the degraded discharge still arrests it. No fire-severity or agent-effectiveness data in the SDD to derive the outcome; classify once the coincident-fire consequence and residual-capability margin are quantified.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing to one engine or APU zone only
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Extinguishing unavailable to one protected zone while remaining zones retain capability; on a fire in the affected zone the aircraft has no discharge into that zone. Engine bottles are cross-plumbed within an engine pair, and the APU has an independent bottle, so loss is confined to the one affected zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew actuate the fire handle for the affected zone with no discharge, while other zones remain protected; elevated workload managing a fire in the unprotected zone and diverting.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect depends on whether a fire occurs in the specific unprotected zone and whether it becomes uncontained. No fire-growth or firewall-containment data in the SDD to derive the outcome; classify once the coincident-fire consequence is established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of agent charge before demand
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Agent charge lost or depleted with no annunciation, so the extinguishing capability is silently unavailable; on a subsequent detected fire the crew actuate the handle expecting discharge and obtain none, with no prior opportunity to plan around the missing protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no awareness the charge is unavailable; on demand they actuate the fire handle and receive no discharge, with a delayed and elevated response to an unarrested fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect depends on a coincident fire in the affected zone and its consequence, made worse by the absence of prior awareness. No fire-growth or containment data in the SDD to derive the outcome; classify once the coincident-fire consequence is established. Whether the loss is genuinely undetectable also needs monitoring/dispatch-check confirmation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of breathing oxygen supply to the crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable, but no protective oxygen is available to the crew for a subsequent loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event or the descent/diversion that follows one.
fha.effCrew: In a concurrent depressurisation, smoke or fume event at maximum operating altitude the crew cannot don a functioning mask; crew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely during the required emergency descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: No effect: the hold is unoccupied in flight and there is no passenger oxygen.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous (for engineer confirmation): with a concurrent depressurisation/smoke event at FL260, absence of crew oxygen produces physical distress or excessive workload such that the flight crew cannot be relied upon during descent/diversion. Severity is driven by the assumed concurrent event; if oxygen is NOT protecting against a credible concurrent condition, revisit. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of delivered oxygen quality
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable, but crew protection is silently ineffective when oxygen is demanded in a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew don masks believing they are protected but receive degraded/contaminated oxygen; in a concurrent depressurisation or smoke event they suffer physical distress or impairment and cannot be relied upon to perform the emergency descent and diversion accurately or completely; the degradation is undetected so no crew action mitigates it.
fha.effPax: No effect: the hold is unoccupied in flight and there is no passenger oxygen.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous (for engineer confirmation): undetected quality degradation gives no annunciation and no compensating crew action, so in a concurrent depressurisation/smoke event the crew suffer physical distress/excessive workload such that they cannot be relied upon. Driven by the assumed concurrent event; confirm the quality-monitoring credit and the concurrent scenario. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen availability to the crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable; reduced oxygen reserve narrows the diversion time available with crew on oxygen following a pressurisation, smoke or fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain oxygen but with reduced reserve/duration; the SDD states either cylinder alone can supply the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve, so residual protection remains but margin against a long diversion is eroded.
fha.effPax: No effect: the hold is unoccupied in flight and there is no passenger oxygen.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD gives redundancy (two cylinders, crossover, per-mask regulators, 'either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve') but does not state how much reserve/diversion-time remains after the partial loss, nor whether that residual meets the required diversion at max operating altitude. Whether this is Major (significant reduction in safety margins) or lower requires the diversion-time and reserve budget the AFHA must establish — not stated in the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen supply to a single mask station
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable; one crew station loses oxygen protection while other stations remain supplied (regulators are independent per mask).
fha.effCrew: The crew member at the affected station has no oxygen in a pressurisation, smoke or fume event; remaining stations stay protected. The effect depends on the crew complement in use (nominal two, provision for four) and whether an unprotected crew member is required for the descent/diversion.
fha.effPax: No effect: the hold is unoccupied in flight and there is no passenger oxygen.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD states 'Regulators are independent per mask' and 'four quick-donning full-face masks', but the aircraft-level effect turns on how many crew are actually aboard (nominal two, provision for four) and whether the remaining protected stations suffice for the emergency descent/diversion. That minimum-crew and task-allocation context is not in the SDD, so effects do not yet drive a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to deliver oxygen on crew donning action
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable; oxygen is unavailable to a donning crew member at the moment it is demanded in a pressurisation, smoke or fume event.
fha.effCrew: On donning, the crew member receives no oxygen flow when it is demanded; the extent of the effect depends on whether the failure is at one station (other stations remain, regulators independent per mask) or across the common manifold, and on the concurrent event driving the demand. The SDD does not distinguish scope for this condition.
fha.effPax: No effect: the hold is unoccupied in flight and there is no passenger oxygen.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the effect depends on the scope of the delivery failure (single station versus common manifold/crossover) and on the concurrent event demanding oxygen. The SDD describes 'a common manifold with a crossover valve' and 'demand regulators' but does not fix the failure scope for this condition, so the effects do not resolve to a single §25.1309 class. Confirm scope and concurrent-event context before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure differential control (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: No control of fuselage differential; structure protected by independent mechanical positive/negative relief. Uncontrolled differential/cabin altitude to the flight-deck compartment; occupied compartment is the flight deck only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.effCrew: Crew lose automatic and any degraded control of differential; must manage cabin altitude by descent and by crew oxygen use; workload and physiological exposure depend on resulting flight-deck cabin altitude, which is not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule and the physiological consequence of losing differential control at FL260 are not quantified in the provided material, and crew oxygen availability/diversion time bounds the outcome but is a separate function. The hold-altitude equivalent is preliminary. Effects therefore do not by themselves entail a specific anchor; left empty for engineering judgement against the ceiling, oxygen and diversion data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced control of pressure differential (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Differential still controlled but at reduced capability; structure remains protected by independent mechanical relief. Cabin altitude held with reduced margin/precision.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain control with reduced margin; increased monitoring; may need altitude restriction. Physiological effect on crew not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: 'reduced control' is not quantified against a cabin-altitude margin or a safety-margin reduction in the provided material, so the effects do not entail a specific anchor (Minor vs Major turns on the magnitude of margin loss, which is not stated). Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous under-pressurisation of the occupied compartment (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Control commands an erroneously low differential; flight-deck cabin altitude rises above intended; negative-pressure relief and structure unaffected. Occupied compartment (flight deck) experiences rising cabin altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew exposed to elevated cabin altitude; annunciated (aware case) and mitigated by crew oxygen donning and descent; workload increase and physiological exposure depend on the magnitude of the cabin-altitude excursion, which is not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the resulting flight-deck cabin altitude for an erroneous under-pressurisation, and the physiological consequence to the crew before oxygen/descent, are not quantified in the provided material. Outcome bounded by crew oxygen (separate function) and FL260 ceiling but the anchor (crew distress/incapacitation vs slight workload) cannot be fixed. Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure differential schedule developing below detection thresholds (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Differential schedule drifts erroneously below crew/monitor detection thresholds; structure protected by independent mechanical relief. Cabin altitude departs intended schedule without annunciation (unaware case).
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; continue normal duties while cabin altitude drifts, until the excursion becomes detectable or reaches a physiological threshold. Result depends on how far the schedule drifts before self-annunciation, which is not quantified in the provided material.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive severity: the undetected drift and its terminal cabin-altitude excursion are not quantified in the provided material, and the unaware case removes crew mitigation, so the physiological outcome bounds severity but is not stated. Left empty; the undetected/unaware nature warrants engineering attention when the cabin-altitude schedule and detection thresholds are defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effAc: Unannunciated thrust change alters trajectory and, if on one side, introduces yaw/roll requiring correction; a large uncommanded change on an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm imposes the directional-control sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the anomaly and counter with rudder/thrust management; workload and reaction time critical near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects vary widely with number of engines affected, magnitude and phase — a small change is a workload item, a large uncommanded outboard change approaches the directional-control sizing case. The SDD does not bound the magnitude or engine count of the uncommanded change, so the worst-case aircraft effect cannot be grounded to a single class. Left empty pending FCS/PRP failure-magnitude data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to a crew thrust command (engine responds other than commanded)
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops a thrust state other than commanded; if asymmetric, yaw/roll and trajectory error result. An erroneous outboard response at the 28 m arm engages the directional-control sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect mismatch between command and response and must re-manage thrust/rudder; error is misleading because the command was made yet the response differs.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — As for the uncommanded case, the aircraft consequence depends on magnitude, sign and which engine responds erroneously — the SDD does not bound these, so the worst-case class cannot be grounded. Left empty pending failure-magnitude/response data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow thrust drift below the crew detection threshold, crew unaware
fha.effAc: Thrust drifts slowly below the crew-detection threshold; with the crew unaware and taking no action, the SDD provides no bounded aircraft-level trajectory or performance consequence.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding the drift, by definition of the unaware condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The condition is defined as below the crew-detection threshold with no crew action; the SDD does not state what aircraft-level effect (e.g. fuel/range, asymmetry, terminal trajectory error) the accumulated drift produces. Without a grounded aircraft effect the condition cannot be classified. Left empty pending drift-magnitude and accumulation-effect data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust (one engine) with resulting directional-control asymmetry, within control authority
fha.effAc: Loss of one engine produces asymmetric thrust and reduced total thrust; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1, with rudder authority sized for the outboard case, so the condition is within available directional-control authority.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply rudder to counter yaw, manage remaining thrust and divert; significant but manageable increase in workload and reduction in performance margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in functional capability and thrust margin plus significant crew workload from the asymmetry, but within the sized directional-control authority and the design one-engine-inoperative continuation case, so a large reduction in safety margins is not reached. Confirm against FCS rudder-sizing evidence. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust with directional-control asymmetry beyond available control authority
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust exceeds the rudder authority sized to the outboard-engine-out case, producing loss of directional control of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest the yaw/roll with available rudder; control is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetry beyond the directional-control authority yields loss of aircraft control, which is loss of the airplane — Catastrophic. The class rests on the assumption that this condition genuinely exceeds the sized rudder authority (e.g. failure of a second engine on the same side, outside the design dispatch case); confirm against FCS/PRP evidence. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust available from any engine; aircraft cannot sustain flight and cannot climb, hold or go around — forced descent to a forced landing/ditching outside a suitable aerodrome in most phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew face a total-thrust-loss emergency with no engine-out recovery available; glide and forced-landing management under severe time pressure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; occupants are flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust in any phase precludes continued flight and leads to a forced landing off-field with likely loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment in flight
fha.effAc: Asymmetric reverse thrust from an inboard engine in flight produces a large yaw/roll upset and loss of directional control; large reduction in controllability, potentially unrecoverable.
fha.effCrew: Sudden departure requiring immediate high-workload recovery with degraded controllability.
fha.effPax: Occupants are flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent in-flight reverse thrust on an inboard engine produces an uncontrollable upset in the vulnerable phases, consistent with loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Yawing moment during the ground roll degrades directional control on a semi-prepared strip; may cause runway/strip excursion depending on speed, surface and available margin.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control with rudder/steering during deceleration.
fha.effPax: Occupants are flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD gives the deceleration margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout) but does not characterise the yaw magnitude, excursion energy, or semi-prepared-surface terrain that would fix the aircraft-level outcome; severity cannot be derived from the effects as stated.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust contribution lengthens the ground roll; wheel braking must absorb more energy, eroding the margin between the 1,800 m landing distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely more heavily on wheel braking; increased attention to stopping performance.
fha.effPax: Occupants are flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reverse thrust is a supplement to wheel braking and the SDD does not quantify the credit reverse thrust takes in the landing-distance case, so the incremental effect on the stopping margin cannot be resolved to an aircraft-level severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust deceleration; the full stopping duty falls on wheel braking against the 1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface; excursion risk if braking is also degraded or the surface is contaminated.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage stopping on wheel braking alone, monitoring the reduced margin.
fha.effPax: Occupants are flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Wheel braking is the primary means of ground deceleration and the SDD credits it independently; the aircraft-level severity of losing reverse thrust alone depends on the braking-only stopping distance versus the strip length, which the SDD does not close out.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of reverse thrust for ground deceleration, unannunciated at deceleration onset
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration provided by wheel braking only; reverse-thrust contribution to stopping distance lost. Reversers are fitted to inboard engines only; wheel braking is an independent means. Effect on total landing/RTO stopping distance and on the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface cannot be quantified from the function definition.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware at deceleration onset (unannunciated); continue normal roll-out expecting reverse contribution, detecting the shortfall only through deceleration feel/margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect sufficient to classify: the reverse-thrust contribution to certified stopping distance, and the resulting margin against the 1,800 m landing requirement with braking-only on a semi-prepared surface, is not stated by the function definition. Requires the landing-performance credit taken for reverse thrust and the braking-only stopping distance to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous aircraft attitude response to crew command in pitch, roll or yaw
fha.effAc: Aircraft attitude responds differently from the crew command in pitch, roll or yaw — loss of predictable trajectory control authority, potentially departing controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew command not honoured as intended; corrective inputs may be ineffective or aggravating, high workload attempting to recover the flight path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8).
