Severity rationale: Erroneous response of the primary attitude-control function can lead to loss of controlled flight — consistent with loss of the airplane. Aligns with the existing committed aircraft-level condition FC-009 (Catastrophic) for erroneous attitude response. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded aircraft attitude motion in pitch, roll or yaw with no crew command
fha.effAc: Attitude departs from the commanded/trimmed state with no crew input — uncommanded excursion in pitch, roll or yaw degrading trajectory control and, if of sufficient rate or magnitude, leading to loss of controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion and arrest it with corrective inputs; elevated workload and potential for the excursion to exceed recoverable limits before correction.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded excursion of the primary attitude-control function can lead to loss of controlled flight — loss of the airplane. Consistent with the committed Catastrophic classification of the related SF-003 attitude-control conditions (FC-009/FC-010). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow uncommanded aircraft attitude divergence below the crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Attitude diverges slowly with no crew command and below the crew-detection threshold; unmitigated divergence accumulates into a departure from the intended flight path with no timely correction.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — continue normal duties and take no corrective action; the divergence is only recognised once it has grown beyond the detection threshold, by which time recovery margin may be lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected slow divergence removes the crew mitigation entirely; an unarrested attitude departure of the primary flight-path control function can lead to loss of controlled flight — loss of the airplane. Matches the existing committed aircraft-level condition FC-010 (Catastrophic). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous aircraft attitude response to crew command below the crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Attitude responds erroneously to crew commands by an amount below the crew-detection threshold; the mismatch is not perceived, so the flight path progressively deviates from intended without correction, accumulating into a departure from the intended trajectory.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the response error — continue commanding normally, taking no compensating action; the error is recognised only once its cumulative effect exceeds the detection threshold, with reduced recovery margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected erroneous response of the primary attitude-control function removes the crew mitigation; an unrecognised, uncorrected error in trajectory control can lead to loss of controlled flight — loss of the airplane. Consistent with the committed Catastrophic classification of the related SF-003 conditions (FC-009/FC-010). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority within controllable limits (pitch, roll or yaw)
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority in one or more axes; aircraft remains controllable within the retained authority, with reduced manoeuvre margin.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly within the degraded authority; degraded control law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects state significant reduction in functional capability / manoeuvre margin while the aircraft stays controllable, and significant increase in crew workload. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority beyond controllable limits (pitch, roll or yaw)
fha.effAc: Retained authority is insufficient to maintain safe flight in the affected axis; control cannot be sustained through the envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest attitude divergence with the authority remaining.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By its stated definition the residual authority is beyond controllable limits, i.e. loss of the airplane is the credible outcome. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of attitude control authority (pitch, roll and yaw)
fha.effAc: No means to control aircraft attitude; aircraft uncontrollable.
fha.effCrew: No control authority available to the crew.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the attitude-control function leaves the aircraft uncontrollable — loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment (flaps/slats develop left/right differently)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric lift and rolling moment during low-speed configuration change; increased directional/roll disturbance requiring correction.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload to counter the rolling moment during a low-speed, high-workload phase.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects state a controllable roll disturbance in a low-speed phase with a significant workload increase; supports Major on the stated effects. Whether an uncontrollable case exists would need the asymmetry magnitude / roll authority margin, which is not given. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement (deployment or retraction without crew command)
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends on the airspeed/flight phase at which the uncommanded movement occurs (e.g. retraction near stall speed vs deployment at high speed vs structural overspeed of the surfaces). The function definition 'provide high-lift for low-speed flight' does not fix the speed/phase context needed to state an aircraft effect, so severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift capability — reduced but symmetric slat/flap deployment
fha.effAc: High-lift still performed at reduced capability; approach and landing flown at an increased speed with a smaller reduction in stall-speed margin than the total-loss case; landing distance increases against the semi-prepared requirement.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing a reduced-configuration approach; performance penalty applied.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects are a reduced-capability version of the total-loss case, but the function definition and SDD do not state the degree of reduction (which flap/slat sections remain) nor its effect on stall margin and landing distance, so the effect magnitude — and hence the class between Minor and Major — cannot be grounded. Missing: the retained-configuration performance/stall-margin data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric high-lift below the crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Asymmetric slat/flap position produces a rolling moment that, being below the detection threshold, is not annunciated; the crew fly on unaware of a persistent roll/lateral-trim demand at low speed.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally and take no action (unaware); a standing lateral control demand at low speed with no cue as to its cause.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The asymmetry-brake architecture bounds gross runaway asymmetry, but neither the function definition nor the SDD gives the roll moment corresponding to a below-threshold asymmetry, so its effect on lateral control margin at low speed — and thus the class — cannot be derived. Missing: the below-threshold asymmetry magnitude and its lateral-control-margin effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground support/flotation configuration indication — configuration indicated correct when it is not
fha.effAc: The aircraft's ground-support/flotation configuration is misindicated as correct; the crew commit to operating on a semi-prepared strip on a false indication, where footprint pressure and support are the sizing basis, without the cue that would prompt rejection.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on erroneous configuration indication and take no corrective action; dispatch/operate decision taken on wrong information with no line maintenance available at the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An erroneous 'correct' indication removes the crew's ability to detect a bad ground-support/flotation state on a semi-prepared surface, but the SDD does not define the ground-support/flotation configuration nor the consequence of operating misconfigured (gear/bogie/footprint), so the aircraft effect magnitude and class cannot be derived. Missing: the configuration that must hold and the consequence of its loss on a semi-prepared surface.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ground support configuration integrity — degradation present, not annunciated, crew unaware
fha.effAc: Ground-support/flotation configuration integrity is degraded but not detected; the crew continue normally and the aircraft operates on a semi-prepared strip with a footprint/support state below that on which the flotation design rests, unannounced.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding the degradation (unaware).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected loss of support-configuration integrity on a semi-prepared surface could compromise support/flotation, but the SDD does not define the configuration integrity that is lost nor the aircraft-level consequence of its undetected loss, so the effect magnitude and class cannot be grounded. Missing: definition of the support-configuration integrity and its failed-state ground consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability — aircraft supported on the ground at reduced capability or on fewer than the full complement of gear/bogies
fha.effAc: Aircraft supported on the ground at reduced footprint/support; load redistributes onto remaining bogies with increased local ground and structural loading; ground handling and directional control on the semi-prepared strip degraded.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to manage degraded ground handling and any dispatch/turnaround decision at a strip with no line maintenance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects can be stated (reduced support, load redistribution, degraded ground handling) but the SDD does not quantify how much support is lost or the resulting excursion/structural consequence against the stated landing margin, so the aircraft-level outcome cannot be pinned to one class. Engineer to classify against ground-loads and excursion consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of adequate flotation on a semi-prepared surface — footprint pressure exceeds what the operating surface can bear
fha.effAc: Footprint pressure exceeds surface bearing capacity on the semi-prepared strip; gear penetration/rutting, risk of bogging, degraded braking and directional traction, and potential excursion from the intended path; on a 1,800 m requirement against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout the available margin is consumed by any traction/rollout degradation.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain directional control and stopping performance on a degrading surface with no diversion to a paved field at the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Flotation is design-sized to the semi-prepared surface and the SDD gives the landing-distance requirement versus predicted rollout as the operating margin, but it does not quantify surface bearing, the degree of flotation loss, or the resulting excursion/entrapment consequence — so the effect cannot be derived to a single class. Engineer to classify against the surface-bearing and excursion case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Braking erroneously applied against crew command — braking action differs from that commanded by the crew
fha.effAc: Braking output differs from the crew command — erroneous or asymmetric braking with degraded/altered stopping and directional behaviour on the ground; on a semi-prepared strip with a 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, an erroneous braking response erodes the stopping/directional margin and risks path deviation or excursion.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to counter the unexpected braking response and maintain directional control, potentially at high ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An erroneous braking response degrading stopping/directional control can be stated, but the aircraft-level outcome depends on which wheels/side and the phase (e.g. asymmetric excursion versus tolerable rollout increase), which the SDD does not resolve — so the class cannot be derived here. Engineer to classify against the directional/excursion consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded brake application with no crew braking command
fha.effAc: Brakes apply with no crew command — unexpected/asymmetric deceleration and yawing moment on the ground; during the take-off ground roll this opposes acceleration and can cause tyre overheat/burst or a path deviation; the semi-prepared surface and the stated stopping margin bound the tolerable case.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an unexpected deceleration and any resulting directional deviation, increasing workload at high ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The uncommanded-braking effect (unexpected deceleration, yaw, possible tyre distress) is grounded, but whether the aircraft-level outcome is a tolerable performance loss or a directional excursion depends on the affected wheels, symmetry and phase — not resolved in the SDD — so severity cannot be derived. Engineer to classify against the worst-phase directional/excursion case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground wheel-braking deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel-braking deceleration available; aircraft relies on inboard reverse thrust only (reversers fitted to two inboard engines) plus aerodynamic drag. On a semi-prepared strip with a 1,800 m landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, loss of the primary deceleration means removes the stopping margin; runway/strip overrun probable, particularly on a rejected take-off at high energy.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect no braking response and have no effective alternate deceleration on the ground roll; high workload with no means to recover stopping distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Overrun off a semi-prepared strip at landing/RTO energy with the stopping margin removed and reverse thrust available on inboard engines only; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking across the wheel groups
fha.effAc: Unequal braking force between left and right wheel groups produces a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to pull the aircraft off the strip centreline; directional-control demand on a semi-prepared surface where surface friction is variable.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the induced yaw through steering and pedal input while decelerating; increased workload and potential for lateral runway excursion if the asymmetry exceeds controllability.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Directional upset from brake asymmetry is credible, but the SDD does not state the magnitude of asymmetry the design permits nor the residual directional authority (nose-wheel steering / rudder) on a semi-prepared surface, so the effect cannot be resolved between a significant reduction in safety margin (Major) and loss of directional control leading to excursion (Hazardous/Catastrophic). Controllability data is missing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded braking effectiveness below crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: A small braking-effectiveness shortfall not evident to the crew; achieved deceleration marginally below scheduled, consuming a portion of the stopping margin without annunciation. On a strip sized near the predicted rollout this erosion goes uncompensated because the crew take no corrective action.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal braking assuming scheduled performance and take no action; the shortfall is only revealed by stopping short of expectation or an overrun.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Below-threshold undetected degradation erodes the stopping margin with no crew compensation, but the SDD does not bound how much undetected degradation is possible before it becomes apparent, so the resulting margin loss cannot be quantified and the class cannot be committed between Minor and Major.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Anti-skid regulation error not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Erroneous anti-skid regulation (releasing or misapplying brake pressure) on a semi-prepared, variable-friction surface without crew awareness; achieved deceleration differs from commanded, potentially reducing stopping performance or inducing wheel behaviour (skid/lock) the crew do not compensate for.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal braking and take no corrective action because the regulation error is not annunciated; degraded stopping or directional behaviour discovered only through outcome.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The direction and magnitude of the anti-skid regulation error (under-braking vs skid inducement) and its effect on stopping distance / tyre behaviour on a semi-prepared surface are not stated in the SDD, so the aircraft effect cannot be resolved and no class can be committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Nose-wheel steering erroneously responds to a crew steering command (steering responds other than commanded) during ground roll
fha.effAc: Erroneous ground track / directional deviation on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout; reduced lateral margin toward the strip edge; rudder provides directional authority at higher ground speed but nose-wheel authority dominates at low speed.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter with rudder/differential braking; increased workload during a high-tempo landing rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in directional-control margin during the ground roll on a length-limited semi-prepared strip, with crew countering by rudder/braking within capability. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel deflection with no crew steering command during ground roll
fha.effAc: Sudden directional deviation from track with no crew input on a length-limited semi-prepared strip; potential runway/strip departure if not immediately countered; low-speed regime is where nose-wheel authority dominates and rudder is least effective.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded deviation and react with rudder/differential braking; workload increase, reaction time critical at low speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects on aircraft are stated but the worst-case outcome (departure at speed vs benign low-speed taxi deviation) depends on speed regime and available counter-authority not resolvable from the SDD; severity left blank pending confirmation of the driving phase and the achievable directional recovery.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Small uncommanded nose-wheel steering bias not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Slow lateral drift from intended ground track that the crew does not perceive as abnormal; gradual reduction in lateral margin correctable by normal directional control inputs on the strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and unconsciously corrects track with routine rudder/steering input; slight workload increase, no discrete alert assumed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Small, sub-threshold bias corrected within normal directional-control inputs; slight reduction in ground-track margin and slight workload increase. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority or range (partial loss of directional control on the ground)
fha.effAc: Reduced steering authority for track corrections on a semi-prepared strip; larger inputs and greater use of rudder/differential braking required to hold track; degraded low-speed manoeuvring but directional control still achievable.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain track with degraded steering authority; use of rudder and differential braking as compensation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground directional-control capability requiring compensation, on a length-limited semi-prepared strip; residual control remains through rudder and differential braking. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric or restricted directional (nose-wheel steering) response during ground roll
fha.effAc: Directional response asymmetric or restricted to part of the commanded range; track deviations toward the restricted side on a semi-prepared strip requiring active compensation; directional control still achievable via rudder and differential braking.
fha.effCrew: Crew must compensate for asymmetric/restricted steering with rudder and differential braking; increased workload during the ground roll.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground directional-control capability from asymmetric/restricted response on a length-limited semi-prepared strip; residual control through rudder and differential braking. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded nose-wheel steering response below crew-detection threshold on the ground
fha.effAc: Ground directional control via nose-wheel steering slightly degraded; degradation is below the crew-detection threshold so the crew take no corrective action and continue duties normally.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level effect: the SDD does not state the consequence of an undetected small steering degradation on tracking/runway-excursion margin on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip, so the effect cannot be sized and severity is left empty rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering directional control on the ground
fha.effAc: Nose-wheel steering directional control lost on the ground; directional control remains available by rudder, differential thrust and differential braking (per-wheel-pair anti-skid), with reduced authority at low ground speed on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain the runway/taxiway centreline using rudder and differential braking; annunciated (crew aware).
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground directional-control capability with significant increase in crew workload, but alternate means (rudder, differential thrust, differential braking) remain; consistent with FC-024 already classified Major in the model. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated locked to the crew when not fully secured
fha.effAc: Nose visor forms the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed; a false locked indication permits dispatch with the door not fully secured, risking in-flight visor departure with loss of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Crew and take-off configuration monitor receive an erroneous locked status and take no corrective action; failure is misleading (crew unaware of the true state).
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path in flight is a plausible path to loss of the airplane; consistent with FC-025 already classified Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated open to the crew when actually secured
fha.effAc: Nose visor is in fact fully secured (pressure boundary and forward load path intact); the erroneous open/unlocked indication fails the take-off configuration check with no actual loss of door integrity.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented a spurious unlocked/open status; increased workload to troubleshoot and dispatch is inhibited by the take-off configuration monitor.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Door is actually secured so there is no in-flight structural or pressure hazard; the effect is a spurious indication causing a slight increase in crew workload and a dispatch interruption. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Incomplete nose-door lock engagement not detected by either sensing path
fha.effAc: Nose visor forms the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed; incomplete lock engagement undetected by both dissimilar sensing paths permits dispatch with the door not fully secured, risking in-flight visor departure with loss of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Neither the proximity sensing harness nor the mechanical indicator linkage reveals the incomplete engagement; crew unaware and take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Common failure of both dissimilar sensing paths leaves an unsecured pressure boundary and forward load path undetected in flight, a plausible path to loss of the airplane; consistent with FC-026 already classified Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded or slowed loading/unloading access to the hold
fha.effAc: Blade loading/unloading is a ground operation; degraded access slows or impedes the ground handling task. No effect stated on the aircraft in flight (hold unoccupied in flight, no in-flight access operation).
fha.effCrew: Increased ground-handling effort/time; no flight-crew task effect in flight.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loading access is a ground operation only (§5.8.6); the function definition supports no in-flight aircraft/crew/occupant effect. This is a dispatch/turnaround availability condition, not a flight-safety effect. Missing: any aircraft-level in-flight consequence to classify against §25.1309. Abstain rather than assign No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of hold loading/unloading access
fha.effAc: Blade cannot be loaded or unloaded; aircraft cannot be dispatched with/without payload as intended. Ground operation only; no in-flight aircraft effect stated.
fha.effCrew: Ground-handling task cannot be completed; no in-flight flight-crew effect.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loading access is a ground procedure (§5.8.6) with the hold unoccupied in flight; the definition supports no in-flight aircraft/crew/occupant effect to classify. Complete loss of access is a ground dispatch/turnaround condition. Missing: any aircraft-level in-flight consequence. Abstain rather than assign No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Payload restraint status erroneously indicated intact when degraded (misleading)
fha.effAc: Crew accept degraded restraint as intact and continue through flight load cases; a restraint degradation persists undetected. Aircraft-level consequence depends on how far restraint degradation can proceed while indicated intact (potential blade shift under flight/landing load cases).
fha.effCrew: Crew take no action on a condition they believe is nominal; no cue to inspect or downgrade the load case.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Misleading indication of an intact restraint on a 72.6 t single unitised blade is a candidate high-severity condition, but the SDD does not state how much restraint can be lost while indicated intact, nor the flight-load-case consequence of an undetected degradation (e.g. whether it can mask loss beyond two adjacent stations). Cannot derive severity without the restraint-loss/load-case consequence. Abstain.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Tension monitoring loop failed such that restraint degradation goes unannunciated
fha.effAc: Loss of the means to detect restraint degradation in flight; a subsequent restraint degradation would proceed without annunciation. Aircraft-level consequence depends on the restraint degradation that can occur undetected while the loop is inoperative.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of a strap-tension loss; crew unaware of any restraint degradation that occurs while the loop is failed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is loss of the monitoring means (single instrumented loop, §5.8.3), not loss of restraint itself. Its aircraft-level severity depends on the probability and magnitude of an underlying restraint degradation occurring undetected during the exposure — not stated in the SDD. Cannot derive severity from the definition alone. Abstain.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint through load cases
fha.effAc: Single 72.6 t unitised blade unrestrained and free to shift longitudinally through flight load cases; large CG excursion and hold-structure/load-path overload; loss of aircraft control likely.
fha.effCrew: Restraint condition annunciated; crew cannot re-restrain in flight (indication only, no in-flight adjustment); no recovery action available.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unrestrained 72.6 t single blade shifting through flight load cases produces a large CG excursion and structural overload of the hold load path, consistent with loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of tension at a single strap station
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap annunciated in flight; indication only, no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so restraint capability is retained; the residual-margin case that would fix the aircraft effect (whether a single-station loss reduces a safety margin) is not stated — cannot classify without it. NSE/Minor not reached for to avoid a blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint degradation outside the tension-loop coverage
fha.effCrew: Degradation outside the monitored coverage is not annunciated; crew continue duties with no indication of the condition.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected restraint degradation where the single tension loop does not provide coverage; the aircraft effect depends on the extent of the coverage gap and the residual load-path margin, neither of which is stated. Coverage-gap analysis required before an effect can be stated or a severity derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous conditioning or pressurisation control response
fha.effCrew: Crew-aware condition; specific crew indication and assumed corrective action (e.g. manual mode selection) not established.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Hold is a low-differential compartment (≈8,800 m equivalent, preliminary); the specific over- or under-pressurisation excursion and its effect on the flight deck occupied zone are not stated. Cannot derive severity without the pressurisation-excursion effect and the flight-deck-vs-hold zoning consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous differential control developing below detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Develops below the detection threshold; crew unaware, continue duties normally and take no action regarding it.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected pressurisation differential excursion on a low-differential hull; the aircraft effect depends on the excursion magnitude relative to the independent structural relief margin, which the SDD flags as preliminary and not frozen. Cannot classify without the excursion magnitude and relief-margin data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of conditioning and air distribution — reduced conditioning capacity or single-zone loss
fha.effAc: Reduced conditioning capacity; single-pack operation permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule per the SDD. Occupied flight deck may see degraded temperature/ventilation but conditioning to the deck is retained via cross-bleed.
fha.effCrew: Possible increased monitoring/reconfiguration workload (select pack configuration/bleed source); no loss of essential crew function stated in the definition.
fha.effPax: None occupied in flight — hold is unoccupied; blade payload only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Definition supports a reduced-capability partial loss with single-pack fallback, but the SDD does not quantify the residual flight-deck conditioning shortfall or its effect on crew task performance across phases, so an aircraft effect severe enough to classify cannot be derived. Missing: the degraded-schedule flight-deck environmental limits and any crew-workload/comfort consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of pressure-differential control within limits — differential still controlled but at reduced capability
fha.effAc: Pressure differential remains within structural/operating limits; control retained through the remaining controller/outflow valve (two controllers, two outflow valves, either sufficient) or pneumatic backup.
fha.effCrew: Increased monitoring; may select manual pressurisation mode. No loss of essential function stated.
fha.effPax: None occupied in flight — hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With differential held within limits and full outflow/controller redundancy plus pneumatic backup, the definition does not establish an adverse aircraft effect; but the SDD does not state the occupied-compartment (flight-deck) altitude/differential consequence of operating in this degraded mode, so severity cannot be derived without reaching for the benign end. Missing: flight-deck cabin-altitude outcome and crew action in the degraded/backup mode.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow loss of pressurisation differential developing below the crew-detection threshold — crew unaware
fha.effAc: Differential decays slowly and undetected; flight-deck cabin altitude rises toward ambient without crew action. Maximum operating altitude is FL260, capped by the low hold differential.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action (unaware). Insidious cabin-altitude rise can produce hypoxia and impaired task performance before recognition; crew oxygen is donned only on crew action, not automatically.
fha.effPax: None occupied in flight — hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware, insidious case can drive a hazardous hypoxia outcome, but the classification turns on the FL260 cabin-altitude/time-of-useful-consciousness relationship and on how far the alerting genuinely fails to annunciate — neither is stated in the SDD. Missing: flight-deck cabin-altitude vs. FL260 exposure, alerting behaviour for slow decay, and the assumed crew oxygen response time. Do not benign-default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution to the occupied compartments
fha.effAc: Total loss of conditioning/distribution to the occupied flight deck; loss of the primary pressurisation air source. Aircraft is limited to FL260 by the low differential, and a descent to a survivable altitude would be required.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck conditioning and, with no conditioning air, loss of the means to maintain the occupied-compartment environment; crew workload rises to manage descent/diversion. Crew oxygen supports smoke/fume and depressurisation events on donning.
fha.effPax: None occupied in flight — hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A total loss affects the occupied flight deck, but whether it forces only an emergency descent (recoverable) or produces an unrecoverable occupied-compartment environment depends on the flight-deck cabin-altitude that results at FL260 and on independent relief/backup behaviour — the SDD gives the differential as preliminary and does not state the resulting flight-deck altitude. Missing: occupied-compartment altitude outcome and descent-profile consequence. Classification cannot be derived without it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous over-pressurisation of the occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Erroneous control commands over-pressurisation of the occupied flight deck. Positive pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system per the SDD, so structural over-pressure is limited by mechanical relief.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware via differential/cabin-altitude indication and can select manual pressurisation mode; workload to reconfigure. Physiological effect on crew depends on the differential reached before relief.
fha.effPax: None occupied in flight — hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Independent positive relief bounds the structural risk, but the aircraft/crew effect turns on the differential and cabin-altitude the occupied flight deck reaches before relief actuates and on the physiological consequence to the crew — not stated in the SDD. Missing: relief-valve set point vs. occupied-compartment limits and the resulting crew physiological effect. Cannot derive severity; do not benign-default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure differential control (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential no longer controlled; structure protected only by independent mechanical positive/negative relief valves; cabin altitude follows ambient toward the FL260 ceiling.
fha.effCrew: Loss detected; crew don quick-donning oxygen masks and initiate emergency descent to a safe altitude; significant increase in workload managing the descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Independent mechanical relief protects structure and crew oxygen is available for the diversion, so effects are a significant reduction in pressurisation margin plus significant crew workload rather than crew incapacitation; proposed Major pending the cabin-altitude-vs-FL260 schedule (preliminary hold differential) to confirm the physiological endpoint. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous under-pressurisation of the occupied compartment (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Differential controlled to an erroneously low value; cabin altitude rises above the intended schedule while structure remains within limits.
fha.effCrew: Cabin-altitude excursion detected; crew don oxygen as required and descend; significant increase in crew workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Occupants are flight crew only, oxygen is available, and the fuselage is a low-differential design with a FL260 ceiling, bounding the excursion to a significant reduction in pressurisation margin with significant workload; proposed Major pending the cabin-altitude schedule. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced control of pressure differential (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Pressure differential still controlled but at reduced capability or with increased difficulty; structure within limits.
fha.effCrew: Crew monitor and, where necessary, intervene; slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Differential remains under control with only a slight reduction in margin and slight workload increase; proposed Minor pending the schedule that fixes the residual control capability retained. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic control of pressure differential with manual reversion available (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Automatic pressurisation control lost; differential managed manually via the available manual mode; structure within limits.
fha.effCrew: Crew revert to manual pressurisation management; slight increase in crew workload for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD confirms a manual mode is available so control is retained by crew action, giving a slight increase in workload; proposed Minor pending confirmation that manual reversion holds the intended cabin-altitude schedule. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure differential schedule developing below detection thresholds (Control fuselage pressure differential)
fha.effAc: Differential schedule drifts erroneously below the crew/system detection threshold; structure remains within limits but cabin altitude departs the intended schedule undetected.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no action regarding the drift until (if) it crosses a detectable threshold.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case: the SDD gives no cabin-altitude schedule, no detection-threshold values, and no data on how far an undetected drift can progress before recognition, so the physiological endpoint and exposure cannot be bounded and the aircraft effect cannot be firmly stated. Severity left empty pending that data — not a No-Safety-Effect finding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous bleed ice protection activation reducing available capacity when not required
fha.effAc: Bleed drawn to ice protection when not required imposes a performance/pack penalty; reduced pack capacity and thrust/bleed margin.
fha.effCrew: Performance penalty applied; crew manage configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is an unrequired bleed/performance penalty; the SDD does not quantify the magnitude of the capacity reduction or its margin impact, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be graded — needs the bleed/performance budget.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous electrical ice protection heating activation reducing available electrical capacity
fha.effAc: Electrical heating drawn when not required consumes electrical capacity; the aircraft-level effect depends on the electrical load budget, which the AFHA cannot state.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Electrical power is a RESOURCE consumed by functions; the aircraft-level consequence of reduced available electrical capacity depends on the electrical budget and margin, which the SDD does not quantify — cannot grade without it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of electrical ice protection across heated zones and elements (aware)
fha.effAc: Reduced ice protection on a subset of electrically heated zones/elements (stabiliser zones, individual probes/ports, windshields); protection retained on remaining zones through cross-bleed/electrical redundancy. In icing, localised accretion possible on the lost zone(s).
fha.effCrew: Lost zone annunciated; crew exits icing conditions / selects manual protection and manages the degraded schedule. Increased workload and monitoring.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Aware partial loss with annunciation and available crew action (exit icing / manual selection) leaves protection on remaining zones; effect is a significant reduction in functional capability and increased crew workload rather than a large reduction in safety margin. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of electrical ice protection on stabilisers, probes and windshields
fha.effAc: Total loss of electrical ice protection for the stabiliser leading edges, all probes/static ports, ice detectors and windshields. In the icing envelope, unprotected accretion on stabilisers and probes degrades control/air-data and windshield visibility; wing/cowl bleed protection is unaffected but stabiliser and air-data sensing are exposed.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated per lost-zone indication; crew must exit icing conditions promptly and manage degraded air-data and reduced forward visibility, with substantially increased workload during descent/approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class without the icing-encounter effect on the aircraft: severity turns on whether unprotected stabiliser and probe accretion within the certification icing envelope produces a large reduction in safety margins/control or misleading air-data (Hazardous or worse) versus a manageable exit under crew awareness (Major). The SDD gives the architecture but not the aerodynamic/air-data consequence of full loss in icing; need the icing-envelope substantiation and worst-phase effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading primary flight, navigation or system information (unaware)
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Primary flight information presented to the crew is erroneous but is not annunciated as invalid; the crew may act on false attitude, airspeed, altitude or system state, driving the aircraft toward a hazardous state (e.g. loss of control, terrain/obstacle proximity, envelope exceedance).
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties and fly the misleading information, taking no corrective action against the fault because it is undetected; correct diagnosis depends on cross-comparison against the independent standby instrument, which shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight information acted upon by the crew can lead to loss of the airplane; the misleading (as opposed to lost) nature removes the crew's cue to revert, so worst-case effects across the flight phases support the top of the scale. Confirm against the air-data/display cross-monitoring and standby-reversion architecture that bounds the exposure. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading primary flight, navigation or system information presented as valid, no fault indication
fha.effAc: Aircraft flown to erroneous flight/navigation state; potential departure from intended trajectory or terrain/traffic clearance while the crew act on false but plausible information
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading information with no cue to distrust it; cross-check against standby is not prompted; recovery depends on independent detection
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary information presented as valid, with no annunciation to prompt cross-check, can lead the crew to fly an erroneous state across critical phases; consistent with FC-040 already classified Catastrophic in the model. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight, navigation and system information
fha.effAc: Reduced information available to fly and navigate; remaining primary/reference sources continue to present valid data via reversionary display selection
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to reconfigure displays and cross-check remaining sources; degraded situational information annunciated
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss leaves valid information available (three display processors, three reference units, reversionary selection); effect is a significant reduction in functional capability and increased workload rather than loss of safe flight; consistent with FC-041 Major in the model. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary flight, navigation and system information with independent standby information available
fha.effAc: Primary presentation lost; independent integrated standby instrument continues to present attitude, airspeed and altitude on the DC essential bus, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries
fha.effCrew: Crew transition to standby instrument; workload increased; reduced information for navigation and system management beyond the standby parameters
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD grounds standby availability (independent integrated standby instrument on DC essential, sharing nothing with the primaries), but the AFHA does not state the residual aircraft/crew effect — the flight phase driving worst case and the workload of operating on standby-only information — needed to derive a class between Major and Hazardous. Engineer to state the residual effect and confirm.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight, navigation and system information
fha.effAc: All primary presentation lost; aircraft continues only on the independent standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude) if available; navigation and system information not presented
fha.effCrew: Crew fly on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude only with greatly increased workload; loss of navigation and system-status information impairs task performance particularly in approach and landing
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary presentation forces flight on the standby instrument alone with loss of navigation and system information; a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload impairing task performance, without loss of the airplane given the independent standby; consistent with FC-043 Hazardous in the model. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous alert presented to the crew (nuisance or false alert with no actual condition)
fha.effAc: Aircraft is nominal but the crew may respond to a non-existent condition; potential unnecessary configuration change or diversion
fha.effCrew: Crew workload increased to diagnose and disposition a false alert; risk of distraction from actual flying task and of eroded trust in the alerting list
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single erroneous/false alert increases crew workload and may prompt an unnecessary crew response but does not itself remove capability; effect is a significant increase in crew workload, not loss of safe flight; consistent with FC-044 handling in the model. Confirm severity and whether an aware/unaware split is warranted. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False fire, overheat or smoke warning presented with no actual event
fha.effAc: Spurious fire/overheat/smoke warning with no real event; a crew response to the warning (engine or APU shutdown, fuel isolation, extinguishant discharge) affects a healthy engine/zone and removes a source of thrust or protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on the annunciation per procedure — increased workload managing a non-existent fire and an unnecessary shutdown/diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unnecessary crew response to a false warning (potential shutdown of a healthy engine / unwarranted extinguishant discharge) is a significant increase in crew workload and a reduction in available capability, not a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate a genuine detected fire, overheat or smoke event
fha.effAc: A genuine fire/overheat in an engine nacelle or APU compartment (high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone) is not annunciated; suppression is not commanded and the fire progresses unchecked in a structural/systems-critical zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally with no warning and take no action against the fire until secondary effects appear, by which time margins are eroded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unannunciated genuine fire in an engine/APU fire zone allows uncontrolled fire progression — a large reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities; not classified Catastrophic absent an established path to loss of the aircraft. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Silent loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection capability with no fault annunciation
fha.effAc: Detection capability is lost with no fault annunciation; a subsequent genuine fire/overheat in a monitored fire zone would go undetected and unsuppressed, with the crew unaware the protection is absent.
fha.effCrew: Crew believe protection is present and take no action; a later fire is met with degraded or no warning.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent, unannunciated loss of detection removes the means to detect a fire in a high-energy fire zone; in combination with a fire it yields a large reduction in safety margins, consistent with a latent condition contributing to a Hazardous outcome. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in one or more monitored zones
fha.effAc: Detection coverage is lost in one or more monitored zones (engine nacelle, APU, bleed duct, gear bay or hold station); a fire or overheat within an affected zone would not be detected.
fha.effCrew: Effect on the crew depends on which zone loses coverage and whether the loss is annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD lists the monitored zones but does not establish the aircraft-level effect of losing detection in a single (unspecified) zone — severity depends on WHICH zone loses coverage, whether the loss is annunciated, and the assumed exposure/reversion. Needs engineering judgement on the governing zone before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage
fha.effAc: Overheat detection is lost specifically on the bleed-duct runs and the main gear bays; a bleed-air overheat/leak or a gear-bay overheat (e.g. hot brakes) would not be annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Crew are not alerted to a developing overheat in the affected runs; effect depends on the assumed detection annunciation state.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms overheat detection is fitted to the bleed-duct runs and gear bays but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of its loss (bleed-duct rupture/overheat propagation vs gear-bay overheat), nor whether the loss is annunciated — severity cannot be derived from the description alone; requires engineering assessment of the overheat threat in these runs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection along the hold (one or more stations)
fha.effAc: Detection at one or more of the nine hold stations lost; because no hold suppression is fitted, hold smoke detection is the sole means of crew awareness of a hold fire. A developing hold fire could go undetected or be detected late in the affected station(s).
fha.effCrew: Crew not alerted to a hold fire in the affected coverage; no annunciation to prompt diversion or descent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect depends on the unsubstantiated premise that the hold carries no combustible load (SDD records hold-suppression-not-fitted as 'an assumption to be substantiated'); severity cannot be derived until that premise and the fire-progression consequence are established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of a detection loop below warning threshold
fha.effAc: A detection loop degrades below its warning threshold without annunciation; latent reduction of detection margin. Engine/APU zones retain dual-loop AND-logic detection, degrading to single-loop on loss of one loop, so detection capability is reduced but not necessarily lost.
fha.effCrew: No fault indication; crew unaware detection margin is reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a latent loss of margin in one loop with the paired loop still providing detection; an aircraft-level severity depends on the residual coverage and exposure the SFHA owns, which the function definition alone does not fix.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge extinguishant into an engine or APU zone on crew command
fha.effAc: On a detected engine or APU fire, the extinguishing means fails to discharge when commanded through the fire handle; the aircraft is left with an uncontrolled fire in a designated fire zone with no means to extinguish it.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands discharge and it fails; no extinguishing available, requiring immediate diversion/landing with an active fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An uncontrolled fire in a fire zone could range from Hazardous to Catastrophic depending on the fire-progression / burn-through case and time-to-land; that consequence is not established by the function definition alone, so severity is left for the engineer to derive.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced extinguishing capability in a protected engine or APU fire zone
fha.effAc: Extinguishing agent/coverage available to a protected zone is reduced; on a coincident fire in that zone, probability of successful first-shot extinguishing is degraded and a fire may not be knocked down on the initial discharge.
fha.effCrew: Crew fire drill and discharge proceed normally; reduced effectiveness may not be evident until a genuine fire fails to respond to discharge.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is contingent on a coincident fire event in the affected zone, and the SDD does not state the residual coverage margin (agent quantity vs. zone volume) after the reduction. Whether reduced (not lost) extinguishing still succeeds against a design fire cannot be established from the function/architecture alone — severity left empty pending the coverage/agent-margin data and the coincident-fire exposure assumption.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing to a single engine or APU zone only, other zones retaining capability
fha.effAc: One protected fire zone loses its extinguishing means while the remaining engine/APU zones retain protection; on a coincident fire in the affected zone only, no active suppression is available for that zone (shutdown/fuel-isolation still available).
fha.effCrew: Crew fire handle for the affected zone commands shutdown and fuel isolation as normal; discharge into that zone is ineffective/unavailable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect requires a coincident fire in the single affected zone; the SDD gives cross-plumbed two-bottles-per-engine-pair architecture but does not state the outcome of an uncontrolled single-nacelle fire without suppression (engine shutdown/isolation vs. burn-through/structural involvement). Severity cannot be derived without that fire-progression basis — left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of extinguishing agent charge before demand
fha.effAc: Extinguishing agent has been lost from one or more bottles but the loss is not annunciated; the crew and configuration believe suppression is available. On a coincident fire, the fire handle discharge delivers no (or reduced) agent to the affected zone, undetected until demand.
fha.effCrew: Crew dispatch and operate believing extinguishing is armed; the shortfall is only revealed when discharge is demanded on a genuine fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Latent condition whose aircraft consequence is contingent on a coincident in-zone fire; combined-probability/effect basis and the fire-progression outcome without agent are not stated in the SDD. This is a latency to carry into the exposure/combination analysis, not a directly classifiable single-condition severity — left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing in all engine and APU zones
fha.effAc: No active extinguishing available in any engine nacelle or the APU compartment. On a coincident engine or APU fire, only shutdown and fuel isolation are available; an uncontrolled fire in a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone may progress to structural or fuel-system involvement with no means to suppress it.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute fire drill (shutdown, fuel shut-off, fire handle) but no agent is delivered; workload and concern elevated with no means to arrest a confirmed fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect is contingent on a coincident engine/APU fire; the SDD identifies nacelles/APU as fire zones (high energy, flammable fluid) but does not state the outcome or timeline of an uncontrolled fire without suppression. Whether an unsuppressed fire is survivable via shutdown alone or progresses to loss of the airplane cannot be derived from the provided material — severity left empty pending fire-progression/particular-risk substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to deliver breathing oxygen to the flight crew on the crew donning action, e.g. during a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event
fha.effAc: Aircraft is airworthy but the crew has no protection against the very hazard that prompted donning; safe continuation depends on immediate emergency descent below a survivable altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew act to don masks and receive no oxygen at the moment of demand; in a decompression at FL260 (max operating altitude) or a smoke/fume event this leaves them incapacitation-exposed with only the time to descend; workload and impairment severe.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect. No passenger oxygen is fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Failure to deliver oxygen on demand coincides with a decompression or fume event that itself prompted donning; crew face physical distress and impaired task performance during the descent, but a survivable emergency descent below FL260-equivalent remains available given the low max operating altitude, so effects support Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of delivered oxygen quality — crew don masks and breathe oxygen of degraded/contaminated quality with no indication of the degradation
fha.effAc: Aircraft airworthy, but the protective function the crew rely on during a decompression or fume event is silently unavailable; no cue prompts the crew to reconfigure or descend on the basis of oxygen state.
fha.effCrew: Crew believe they are protected and continue their duties or manage the precipitating event while progressively hypoxic/impaired from degraded oxygen; the absence of any quality indication removes the opportunity to detect and act, driving impaired or lost task performance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected degradation means the crew take no corrective action and are impaired precisely when performing the safety-critical descent/diversion; effects reach physical distress and excessive workload impairing crew task performance. Whether progression to loss of both crew is credible enough to drive Catastrophic depends on quality-degradation kinetics and detection that the SDD does not quantify, so classified Hazardous pending that data. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen availability to the crew — supply present but at reduced quantity/duration below the sized diversion reserve
fha.effAc: Aircraft airworthy; protective oxygen available but with reduced endurance, constraining the time available for descent and diversion after a decompression or fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew are protected but with reduced reserve; workload increases to manage a shortened diversion and to monitor cylinder state, with a possible earlier descent decision. Reduced margin rather than immediate incapacitation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced availability degrades the reserve that sizes the diversion but does not remove protection at the moment of demand; effects are a significant reduction in functional capability / increase in crew workload, supporting Major. Cylinder pressure is displayed and is a dispatch item, so the crew retain awareness. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen supply to a single crew mask station with the remaining stations available
fha.effAc: Aircraft airworthy; oxygen remains available to the other mask stations. With a nominal complement of two and provision for four, a single lost station reduces but does not eliminate crew protection.
fha.effCrew: The crew member at the affected station has no oxygen at that station and must relocate to or share a functioning station; workload and coordination increase during a decompression or fume descent. Regulators are independent per mask, so the fault is confined to one station.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single-station loss removes protection for one crew member at the point of demand but functioning stations remain and regulators are independent per mask; effects are a significant increase in crew workload / reduction in capability during the event, supporting Major. Whether the affected pilot can be re-protected in time depends on flight-deck layout and procedure not stated in the SDD. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of breathing oxygen supply to the flight crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains airworthy but the crew have no protection against a decompression, smoke or fume event; survival depends entirely on an immediate emergency descent below a survivable altitude before crew impairment.
fha.effCrew: On a decompression at up to FL260 or during a smoke/fume event, the crew are wholly unprotected and face hypoxia/incapacitation; a single event that both causes the decompression and coincides with oxygen unavailability can lead to loss of both crew.

fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of crew oxygen is only a hazard in combination with a precipitating decompression/fume event; given the low maximum operating altitude (FL260) a survivable emergency descent remains available, so the loss alone supports Hazardous (large reduction in safety margins, crew physical distress). Whether the combined decompression-plus-oxygen-loss case is Catastrophic must be assessed at PSSA against the two cylinders' independence and the descent time available; classified Hazardous pending that combination analysis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.
